newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Mexico's TMM in joint shipping venture.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's TMM in joint shipping venture.

text.p: Mexican transport giant Transportacion Maritima Mexicana SA (TMM) launched a joint venture with Colombia's Flota Mercante Grancolombiana in Bogota Friday.
TMM will pay $20 million for a 60 percent stake in the new shipping company, Transportacion Maritima Grancolombiana. The remaining 40 percent stake will be owned by Flota Mercante Grancolombiana.
The new company will look to consolidate and expand Flota Mercante Grancolombiana's existing route structure, TMM said in a press statement.
TMM executive chairman Jose Serrano said it was likely the newly-formed company would be floated on the Bogota stock exchange and on Wall Street in the near future.
"We want to make the (new company) efficient and in the not too distant future float it on the stock market," Serrano said at the deal-signing ceremony.

TMM, established more than 40 years ago, is the largest multimodal land and sea transport company in Latin America. But investors are growing increasingly worried about how it plans to pay for a spate of recent acquisitions and new ventures, including the $1.4 billion purchase of a major Mexican railroad network, the Wall Street Journal said Friday.
TMM is paying $10 million cash for its stake in Transportacion Maritima Grancolombiana, the remainder will be financed, according to a TMM spokesman.

The powerful coffee conglomerate Grupo Cafetero, headed by the National Coffee Growers' Federation, has an 80 percent stake in the Flota Mercante Grancolombiana, established 50 years ago. The other 20 percent stake is held by Ecuadoran bank Banco de Fomento de Ecuador.
Both groups have in the past sought to sell off part of their share in Grancolombiana.
Neither succeeded in finding buyers given that the company was racking up gross losses of about $60 million a year against the backdrop of falling real term cargo rates and a declining market share.

Grancolombiana chairman Luis Fernando Alarcon and TMM's Serrano said their companies' entire fleets would be at the disposal of the new company depending on how business expanded. Initially, however, the new venture will employ 170 staff and operate seven leased vessels, according tothe TMM statement.
TMM currently plys routes to 43 countries and 65 ports around the world. Grancolombiana's activities center on Latin America.

Alarcon said the new company would look to develop Pacific coast shipping routes between South America, the United States and Canada and intercontinental routes to the Far East, northern Europe and the Mediterranean.
"The forces of competition have encouraged us to redefine and restructure our operations with the aim of competing on an equal footing with industrialized nations," Alarcon said.
Transportacion Maritima Grancolombiana will be based in Bogota and have offices in all the Colombian ports, New York, Tokyo and Rotterdam.
"This gives us a great opportunity to offer integrated services to our clients," Serrano said.
